title: Noetherian adic formal systems and coherent open ideals
statement: A Noetherian adic formal scheme, using ordinary schemes [def-pc-scheme], with specified ideal of definition is represented by the increasing system $F_n$ of its closed infinitesimal thickenings, $n\geq0$. A formal affine chart is the cartesian system of open immersions $\operatorname{Spec}(B/K^{n+1})\to F_n$, for a Noetherian ring $B$ complete and separated for the powers of its ideal $K$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] [pqf-def-locnoeth]; finitely many such charts cover every $F_n$. This is the infinitesimal-system description of the ringed space $\operatorname{Spf} B$ with its completed structure sheaf. Morphisms preserve the specified filtration. A coherent open ideal is a compatible family of coherent ideal sheaves $J_n$ [pqf-def-coherent] whose closed subschemes factor through $F_N$ for some $N$, at every $n\geq N$; the center is the ordinary closed scheme $V(J_N)$. Regularity means regularity of all complete affine chart rings [def-weil-regular-scheme]. The completion of a scheme $X$ along $I$ is the actual system $V(I^{n+1})$, and a completed ideal is its pullback to each of these schemes. A formal blowup along an open coherent ideal is characterized on every formal affine chart by first blowing up $\operatorname{Spec}B$ in the corresponding supported coherent ideal and then completing along the extended $K$ [def-nagata-global-blowup]; the isomorphism is over that chart. Empty charts, empty covers, and zero or unit ideals are allowed. Reducedness means reduced complete chart rings [def-pc-reduced-scheme], and quasi-excellence means quasi-excellent complete chart rings [def-exc-excellent-ring].
